status: Scoped durable JSON import and recovery notice accepted locally. Whole-wallet durability, remaining screen/accessibility work and final production release gates remain open.
behavior: JSON backup input is cloned before joining the shared password/import queue. Detached decoding verifies supported key type/encoding, address/header, embedded PKCS8 public key and signing proof before conditional acknowledged storage or observable publication.

New records use the current live master password. Readable duplicates retain their exact stored ciphertext and metadata; unreadable or corrupt stored key material is refused and retained. Storage errors and locked late completions propagate as native Error objects through the actual extension message serializer.

Incoming metadata is retained inert in jsonBackupMeta; active identity and legacy-import provenance come from the decoded primary key. Only an explicit caller argument can link an already acknowledged, durable local EVM private key.

Verified default-root entropy enables mnemonic recovery/enrollment. Valid custom-path or unrelated entropy is preserved with the primary signing key but flagged unverified, excluded from automatic network enrollment and mnemonic/raw-seed offers, and shown as JSON-only recovery in all four shipped locales.
Real ethers keystores use the shared awaited local import. Legacy no-algorithm Ed25519, raw-key backups and 20-byte Ethereum address headers retain supported compatibility.

findings.description: Encrypted entropy can belong to a different phrase than the validated primary public/private key. Promoting it as a master phrase misrepresents recovery and can enroll unrelated network accounts. Valid historical custom derivation paths omit their path, so rejecting every non-default root also loses legitimate recovery compatibility.
findings.status: Root reproduced the entropy and metadata findings in json-account-import-storage-independent-before.log (5 failures, 30 filtered skips). Final decoder proves default-root entropy when possible; otherwise it retains the encrypted entropy and validated primary key with internally derived isMnemonicUnverified, suppresses master status/mnemonic export/automatic enrollment, and publishes a visible JSON backup notice. Four custom-path key types preserve their exact signing material and encrypted recovery entropy through password rotation.

findings.description: Passive file metadata previously claimed an unrelated stored Ethereum address and universal network identity; existence of a referenced local account does not authorize a backup to claim it.
findings.status: Final decoder keeps old metadata inert in jsonBackupMeta, derives active primary identity itself, and defaults provenance to legacy-import. A separate explicit linkedEthereumAddress argument is passed only after caller acknowledgement and verified against an actual durable, local EVM private key. Existing duplicate metadata remains authoritative.

findings.description: Installed keyring can derive a public key from a 32-byte private seed while ignoring the PKCS8 embedded public key; that makes header/derived-key equality alone insufficient. A corrupted stored private key must also fail duplicate import.
findings.status: Root reproduced two raw-key PKCS8 cases plus one corrupted stored-private-key duplicate (3 failures, 41 filtered skips). Final JSON decoder always verifies embedded PKCS8 public-key equality and sign/verify proof; LocalAccountImport also proves the stored private key before preserving/publishing a duplicate.

findings.description: The inherited plain {error: message} rejection lacked Error.message used by the top-level response serializer, causing malformed backup failure to appear as an empty successful response.
findings.status: d5371967 removes the catch that changes native Error objects. The explicit regression requires an Error instance and the compiled Chrome harness preserves the prior observed failure. Independent review confirms the error shape now matches handlers/index.ts response serialization.

otherDisposition: Restore captures a detached input before entering the existing shared password/import queue, validates detached key material, and uses the previously qualified durable conditional import path. No publication or account selection occurs before acknowledged key persistence; tested post-write lock veto remains in that path.

Unreadable existing accounts are preserved and rejected rather than replaced; readable duplicates preserve existing encrypted material. New or migrated writes use the current queue-protected master password and conditional storage checks.
The decoder rejects unsupported encoding/type, malformed header/public/private combinations and wrong passwords; legacy no-algorithm Ed25519 and valid Ethereum address-header forms are retained.

Final notices exist in all four shipped web locales. The Akkadian/Egyptian wording composes existing localized labels and backup instruction; this review verifies resource presence and wiring, not linguistic certification.

The browser harness reads the actual restored account flag, exercises main/export views at 100/200 percent in all four locales, and checks horizontal containment. Root owns final execution and raw visual acceptance.
limits: No reviewer execution of web code and no independent final browser image acceptance in this source-review record. Root maintains final full-suite, type, lint, build, packaging, browser and exact source/evidence pins.

Current-account/network preference persistence and multi-account bundle restore are not made a crash-atomic transaction by this change. A successfully persisted separate EVM import can remain if subsequent primary import fails.

limits: Failure/delayed acknowledgement adapters are modeled, including Chrome and IndexedDB. Real Chrome proves successful callbacks and clean runtime reload; abrupt process death/physical disk failure is not simulated.

Fixture deletion removes only the five disposable generated records to model an off-device backup. It does not qualify production deletion/reset. Installed keyring tests exclude unused development nobody fixture and repeated singleton UI initialization; compiled Chrome has neither substitution.

Independent key or preference writes and bundle restore are not atomic as a whole. A separately acknowledged EVM key may remain if the following primary import fails. External/mobile/session/current selection/deletion/reset and general password partial-failure recovery are subsequent gates.
